# CSV export

The stockroom takes calls to export_rows(items). Each item starts as (name, count).
Output uses CSV with a header of name,count. Each name must survive intact, including
commas and quotes. Preserve order and all records. The tool uses Python's standard library.

| Rule | What prevents or detects a violation |
| --- | --- |
| Export preserves names including punctuation | The export round-trip test in tests/test_stock.py. |

## Release notes

The February export split names containing commas. The release candidate should cover
the same failure so it does not come back. Reproduction name: Large, blue.
files.stock.py:
def export_rows(items):
    return "name,count\n" + "".join(f"{name},{count}\n" for name, count in items)

import csv
import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
from stock import export_rows

items = [("Large, blue", 3), ('Screw "A"', 4), ("Washers", 9)]
records = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(export_rows(items))))
assert records == [["name", "count"], *[[name, str(count)] for name, count in items]], records
